newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy defends role in PLO-Israel crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy defends role in PLO-Israel crisis.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk denied in remarks broadcast on Tuesday that Washington was neglecting a two-month-old crisis in Israel-PLO peacemaking.
"If we were taking a hands-off approach, I don't think Ambassador Ross would be spending all his time out here trying to get the parties together," Indyk told Israel's army radio.
U.S. President Bill Clinton's special Middle East envoy Dennis Ross has been in the region trying to arrange a meeting of the two sides.
Israeli news reports have said Washington does not have the political will for the tough moves needed to revive peacemaking.
"We'll be intensively engaged over the next few days and we'll see. It's very difficult, but hopefully we'll make some progress," Indyk said.

Negotiations have been largely stalled since Israel started a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18 and a Palestinian bomber killed himself and three Israeli women at a Tel Aviv cafe on March 21.
Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) officials said on Monday their representatives would attend a meeting with Israelis arranged by Ross, but they emphasised it would not constitute negotiations.

Ross was due to meet Israel's Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai on Tuesday. A Mordechai spokesman said he was checking radio reports Mordechai would lead the Israeli side to talks with Palestinians sometime this week at Indyk's Tel Aviv home.
The radio said Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak's adviser Osama al-Baz would make a lightning visit to Israel this week for talks with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on reviving the negotiations.
An Israeli official who declined to be identified said "there is a possibility of that" but nothing had been set.

Palestinians are demanding a halt to Jewish settlement building in East Jerusalem, the rest of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, areas where they envisage an independent state. Israel wants Palestinians to crack down on militants opposed to peace.

Israel's Haaretz newspaper said last week that Clinton was not interested in a head-on collision with Netanyahu on the issue of a settlement freeze, fearing a confrontation with the U.S. Congress and with the U.S. Jewish community.

The daily said this was despite the fact that Clinton and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright were dissatisfied with Netanyahu's continuing Jewish settlement building, which they viewed as harming peace moves.

Netanyahu said on Sunday he was proud of his March decision that sent bulldozers to carve out the new Jewish settlement of Har Homa on a hilltop in East Jerusalem which Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim.
Ross's mission to the region is his second in a month and has taken him to Jordan and Egypt as well as Israel and Palestinian self-rule enclaves.

PLO officials have criticised Washington for what they said is its refusal to press Israel to halt settlement activities in Palestinian areas during mediation to restart the talks. Israel says it will not stop settlements.
